note: Five pine-shaded campgrounds (Medicine, A.H. Hogue, Hemlock, Headquarters, Schonchin Springs) on the north shore of Medicine Lake in the Medicine Lake Highlands, with a swim beach, boat ramp and dock; the Medicine and A.H. Hogue loops have the larger RV sites. The Medicine loop is closed for a tribal gathering for 5-6 days around the third weekend of July. --Claude
summary: Medicine Lake: $15, 86 sites across five campgrounds, 15 reservable July 1 - Sept 25 on rec.gov, rest first-come, 14-day limit; traditionally July 1 into October, now on winter operations (first-come, water/trash/dump off). Lakefront kept on A.H. Hogue's shore sites.
flags: WATERFRONT: lakefront KEPT, on the A.H. Hogue loop: sites 051 (41.58589,-121.59137) ~17 m, 050 (41.58587,-121.59158) ~23 m, 043 (41.58614,-121.59327) ~22 m and 049 (41.58592,-121.59174) ~32 m from the waterline over open sand with scattered pines; gentle beach shore. The stored evidence's '~40 m' Medicine-loop apron measures ~58-63 m (sites 015 41.58691,-121.59607 and 016 41.58681,-121.59565), so the Medicine loop alone would be lakeview - the call rests on A.H. Hogue. Medicine Lake is a natural lake; the pale beach band is narrow at Hogue.

SCOPE: the entry stands for the whole recreation area (one recreation.gov facility, five campgrounds); the pin sits in the Medicine loop. Headquarters (~1.7 km W, sites 001-010 around 41.5850,-121.6159) and Schonchin Springs are separate campgrounds on their own spurs - split candidates only if wanted; Hemlock adjoins A.H. Hogue.
